name: Mai Chau
provinceNote: Xã Mai Châu has been in Phú Thọ since the 2025 merger (Resolution 202/2025/QH15 and Resolution 1676/NQ-UBTVQH15, governments from 1 July 2025).
dotReason: Worth it if you are already nearby
summary: A green valley of rice fields and Thai stilt-house villages, a short trip west of Hanoi. Sleep in a homestay in Ban Lac or Pom Coong, walk through the fields, and eat bamboo-tube rice and hill chicken at the family table. One night suits families and anyone wanting countryside close to the capital.
timeNeeded: A night and the next morning
getThere: About 140 km from Hanoi; about three hours, and also 2.5 hours
bestMonths: September to November, and March to May
seoTitle: Mai Chau travel guide — a night in the rice valley
seoDescription: Sleep in a White Thai stilt house above the rice, about 140 km from Hanoi. The road is about three hours, and also 2.5 hours. October is one golden window.
intro: The morning is the rice and the roofs. Bản Lác and Pom Coọng are the White Thai stilt-house villages on the valley floor, and the night is a house there, with the fields at the edge and the limestone ridge behind. Stay if that is the trip you booked. Pù Luông is the trek from this valley, a full day on Vietnam Tourism’s wording, and a half day is too short for it. Mộc Châu is the next highland on the same highway, past this valley, and it is its own night.

Give the quiet hour of the morning to the lanes. Look for a drink stall and have cà phê phin looking at the rice, then take a bicycle on the paths between the houses and the paddies. Weaving sits in front of the houses and under the floors. The Sunday morning market is the morning when people come in formal dress and the cloth is sold. The hour is Check on arrival. Electric carts are the other way between villages. The hire for a cart is Check on arrival.

The evening is the stilt-house floor. After dinner, White Thai music and dance. In Pom Coọng the programme named is xòe, sạp, and instruments. Khắp Thái is part of the evening exchange. Travelers fall asleep early under countryside dark. A start time and a closing time are Check on arrival, and so is a separate ticket for the show. Bản Lác holds a cultural night market on Saturday evening, in xã Mai Hạ. The hour and the fee are Check on arrival. Pà Cò’s Sunday morning market, and the Saturday night market at Bản Chà Đáy, are the highland markets, a different morning from the valley’s Sunday market.

Hang Kia and Pà Cò are the Hmong highland of this stay, now xã Pà Cò, about 30 km from the old township on National Highway 6 toward Sơn La, then about 6 km between Bản Chà Đáy and Hang Kia village. Bản Chà Đáy is printed at 1,140 m. Spring brings plum and peach, and a cloud sea, on the rural-tourism feature. The reserve around those villages prints two areas, 1,000 ha and 7,091 ha, and two dates for Decision 194/CT, 8 August 1986 and 9 August 1986. The highest point in that text is 1,536 m. That summit is a different number from the village at 1,140 m. A gate fee and a walking hour are Check on arrival.

The caves are named and still thin as a visit. Hang Piềng Kẻm is a national scenic site by Decision 39/2005/QĐ-BVHTT of 22 August 2005, then in xã Chiềng Châu, now inside xã Mai Hạ. Hang Chiều is called one of the national-level relics, with a repair planned for 2026–2030. Hang Nà Lằn, at xóm Chà Đáy, is the cave visitors like late in the day, for sun through the mouth. Hang Khoài is named in the same sentence, at xóm Bin, without its own hour. Lengths, stair counts, fees, and opening hours are Check on arrival. Dinner is the house, not a restaurant street. The plates are on the food guide.
gettingAround: The usual start is Hanoi. No Mai Châu airfield is named on the Vietnam Tourism or Phú Thọ tourism pages. Nội Bài is the airport those journeys use, then the road through Hòa Bình and National Highway 6. Minutes from the airport are Check on arrival. No Mai Châu station is on the national tourism railway note, which prints Ga Hà Nội at 120 Lê Duẩn. Rail duration is Check on arrival.

The Vietnamese Vietnam Tourism page and the Phú Thọ tourism list both print about 140 km. Vietnam Tourism prints about three hours by car or bus, via Hòa Bình. The northern Vietnam piece prints 2.5 hours in parentheses. Keep both. A Nội Bài information page prints about 150 km in the intro, 130 km from central Hanoi, and 157 km from Nội Bài. Those three disagree with each other and with 140 km. A bus leaves from Mỹ Đình, and a shuttle, a private car, or a motorbike are the other ways named. Local buses run to Mai Châu town, a short walk from Bản Lác and Pom Coọng. A traveler from Sơn La or Điện Biên should ask the driver to stop at the Mai Châu turn-off. The fare and the operator clock are Check on arrival. The morning is the better time to drive, for the view at đèo Thung Khe. A pass fee is Check on arrival.

On the valley floor the bicycle is the way between the stilt houses and the paddies. The Phú Thọ tourism list prints bicycle hire at 20.000–50.000 đồng a trip. No second source printed that price. Electric-cart hire is Check on arrival. The same list prints “Mở cửa 24h” for the valley. That reads as a directory flag, not a ticket gate. A walking fee is Check on arrival. Núi Đầu Rồng is the viewpoint for the whole valley, early morning mist and afternoon cloud. Minutes from the homestay are Check on arrival. June to August monsoon can flood local roads, and heavier rain is also printed from May to September. A closure calendar is Check on arrival.

stayAreas.name: Ban Lac
stayAreas.summary: The main cluster of White Thai stilt houses, on the flat lanes between the roofs and the paddies. Báo Hòa Bình’s rural feature calls the village more than 700 years old, with foreign guests from the 1960s. It places Bản Lác in xã Chiềng Châu. Báo Phú Thọ places it in xã Mai Hạ, the commune formed from Chiềng Châu, Vạn Mai, and Mai Hạ. Both names stay. The town bus drop is a short walk. Vietnam Tourism prints about 200.000 đồng for a rustic homestay, about 600.000 for a boutique farm stay, and about 1.500.000 for a four-star hotel. Those bands are one source.

stayAreas.name: Pom Coong
stayAreas.summary: The second White Thai village, quieter than the main homestay cluster, in the center of xã Mai Châu. Older accounts place it in the township. The name is hill plus drum. About 70 households and more than 300 people. Houses of bamboo, wood, or bương stand about 2 m off the ground, with weaving under the floor. Sleep here when you want the same valley and a smaller lane. The Phú Thọ foreign-affairs page counts 45 community homestays, 15 guesthouses, and 3 hotels in the commune. A 2022 feature counts more than 200 lodging businesses in the old district. The geography and the year differ.

eat: Dinner is the homestay table in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng: cơm lam from the bamboo tube, gà đồi, pork skewers, xôi nếp, and rượu cần. Bản Hịch, about 12 km from the old district center, names vịt đầu xanh, rau sắng, and cá dầm xanh. Hang Kia names xôi nếp nương, lợn bản, gà nướng, and bánh dày. A stall price is Check on arrival. The list is on the food guide.
interestsBody: The night is a rice valley and a stilt-house floor, closer to Hanoi than the high terraces. Dinner is that house. Weaving is under the floor and at the Sunday market.

body: The meal is the house in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng. Vietnam Tourism names cơm lam, gà đồi, thịt lợn xiên nướng, and stuffed fried cicadas. The Phú Thọ tourism list adds vịt cỏ, lợn cắp nách, lợn mán, gà nướng, dế nướng, xôi nếp, rượu cần, rượu Mai Hạ, nhộng ong rừng, and măng chua. Bản Hịch names vịt đầu xanh, rau sắng, and cá dầm xanh. Hang Kia names xôi nếp nương, lợn bản, gà nướng, and bánh dày. A 2019 feature adds cá suối, cá suối chiên, canh cải mèo, trâu gác bếp, and chẩm chéo. A price is Check on arrival.

body: Bản Lác is the main homestay lane. Pom Coọng is the quieter village in the center of xã Mai Châu, a short walk or a bicycle from the town bus drop. Bản Văn is the next hamlet on that walk, with stilt rows and a wider green. Nà Phòn is named as a Thai community village inside xã Mai Châu. A separate hour for each hamlet is Check on arrival.

The bicycle hire on the Phú Thọ tourism list is 20.000–50.000 đồng a trip, one source. The paths run between the houses and the paddies. A motorbike is the road from Hanoi, and the bicycle is the advice for the floor.

blocks.heading: White Thai cloth
paragraphs: Weaving is under the stilt houses and in the lanes, and the Sunday morning market is when the cloth is sold. The hour is Check on arrival. The Phú Thọ foreign-affairs page also names OCOP rượu ngô, tỏi tía, and a sâm planting at Chà Đáy. Those are products of the commune. A shop fee is Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Hang Kia and Pa Co
paragraphs: This is the Hmong highland of the same stay, now xã Pà Cò, formed from Cun Pheo, Hang Kia, Pà Cò, and the rest of Đồng Tân. Nearly 30 km from the old township on National Highway 6 toward Sơn La, then about 6 km from Bản Chà Đáy to Hang Kia village. Bản Chà Đáy is printed at 1,140 m. The Saturday night market is there, and the Pà Cò market is Sunday morning. Hours are Check on arrival. Spring plum and peach, a cloud sea, and Hmong weaving and dyeing are the season the rural feature describes, with no civil dates. A waterfall near the Pà Cò community village is named separately from thác Gò Lào. A fee is Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: Caves in the valley hills
paragraphs: Hang Piềng Kẻm is ranked a national scenic site by Decision 39/2005/QĐ-BVHTT of 22 August 2005. Hang Chiều and Hang Láng are named by Báo Phú Thọ. Hang Mỏ Luông is on the Phú Thọ tourism list and in Báo Phú Thọ. Hang Nà Lằn is the late-afternoon cave, for sun through the mouth, at xóm Chà Đáy. Hang Khoài is at xóm Bin. A length, a stair count, a fee, and an opening hour are Check on arrival.

blocks.heading: A family night on the floor
paragraphs: One night in the house, a bicycle in the morning, and an early dark. After dinner the floor is White Thai music and dance, xòe and sạp in Pom Coọng, and khắp Thái in the evening exchange. Keng Loóng, the pestle dance on a wooden trough, is national intangible heritage of the Thai in this district, performed at Xên Mường and at the evening exchange. The November 2023 ministry decision is described in the article, and the decision number is not printed there. A show ticket is Check on arrival.

Xên Mường is annual in the first lunar month, on the 9th and 10th. Báo Phú Thọ prints the 2026 opening on 26 February, the 10th, in xã Mai Hạ. The ministry records a reception on 19 February 2024, also the 10th, then in the district, at the Tướng Sứ shrine in xóm Chiềng Châu. The next civil date moves. Check on arrival for the next year’s day. Offerings named in 2026 include buffalo, pigs, chickens, sticky rice, wine, and two decorated buffaloes. A ticket is Check on arrival. Xên bản, lễ mừng cơm mới, lễ Chá chiêng, and the Hmong Gầu Tào are named rites. Their next civil dates are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Mai Chau, Pu Luong, or Moc Chau?
faqs.a: Stay in Mai Chau when the morning is a rice valley and a White Thai stilt house, about 140 km from Hanoi. Ride to Pù Luông when you want the trek Vietnam Tourism calls a full day. Continue to Mộc Châu when the tea plateau past the pass is the night you booked. Minutes from Mai Châu to either neighbor are Check on arrival.

faqs.q: How long is the road from Hanoi?
faqs.a: About 140 km, on the Vietnamese Vietnam Tourism page and the Phú Thọ tourism list. Vietnam Tourism prints about three hours by car or bus, via Hòa Bình. The northern Vietnam piece prints 2.5 hours. A Nội Bài information page prints about 150 km, 130 km from central Hanoi, and 157 km from the airport. The bus leaves from Mỹ Đình. The fare is Check on arrival.

In a stilt house in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng. Bản Lác is the main cluster. Pom Coọng is quieter, in the center of xã Mai Châu, with about 70 households. Vietnam Tourism prints about 200.000 đồng, about 600.000 đồng, and about 1.500.000 đồng for a rustic homestay, a boutique farm stay, and a four-star hotel. The commune count and the old-district count disagree, and both are on the stay lines above.

Vietnam Tourism calls September to November the harvest, with October the golden month, and March to May the other pleasant window. Báo Phú Thọ says the rice starts to turn gold in late May and early June, and is gold again in September and October. Heavier rain is printed from May to September, and June to August monsoon can flood local roads. A closure calendar is Check on arrival.

Annual in the first lunar month, on the 9th and 10th. In 2026 the opening was 26 February, the 10th, in xã Mai Hạ. The 2024 reception was 19 February, also the 10th. The next year’s civil date is Check on arrival. A ticket is Check on arrival.

season.note: September to November is the harvest window Vietnam Tourism prints, with October named as the golden month, and March to May the other pleasant months. Báo Phú Thọ says the rice starts to turn gold in late May and early June, and is gold again in September and October. Heavier rain runs from May to September, and June to August monsoon can flood local roads. Drive in the morning for the pass view. A road closure is Check on arrival. Xên Mường falls on the 9th and 10th of the first lunar month. In 2026 the opening was 26 February. The next civil date is Check on arrival.
